primitives.name: Advisory Transaction Lock
primitives.verbatim_quote: **No concurrency story.** `ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1` then INSERT on a Vercel cron will fork or collide under concurrent sport workers.
primitives.assumptions: Multiple writers attempting simultaneous insertion into a shared sequence space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Race condition singularity where overlapping transactions corrupt ordering.

layer2.mapping: Derived from distributed consensus protocols ensuring exclusive access during critical sections.

primitives.assumptions: Candidate keys guarantee entity uniqueness across the entire ledger.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Constraint violation singularity triggering conflict resolution.

The core failure mode is concurrent writer collisions corrupting the ordered audit trail. A Postgres append-only table provides durability but lacks built-in isolation. Advisory locks enforce mutual exclusion at the transaction boundary, transforming the non-atomic `SELECT/INSERT` into an atomic CAS operation. Multi-column unique constraints serve as secondary guards against race conditions, triggering retries rather than silent overwrites. The frozen hash contract ensures that historical entries remain verifiable under unchanged rules, preventing protocol divergence. Together, these primitives form a resilient, append-only ledger resistant to both accidental corruption and malicious tampering.
